problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of inspections across seven regional warehouses, each situated at specific grid coordinates on a district map.  
Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at (29,122)  
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at (187,61)  
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at (12,78)  
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at (45,133)  
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at (186,18)  
Warehouse Zeta: Positioned at (77,103)  
Warehouse Theta: Positioned at (84,76)  

Travel distances between warehouses, measured in kilometers, are predetermined:  
Alpha to Gamma: 47.2 km  
Alpha to Delta: 19.4 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 188.3 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 51.6 km  
Alpha to Theta: 71.7 km  
Beta to Gamma: 175.8 km  
Beta to Delta: 159.2 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 43.0 km  
Beta to Zeta: 117.7 km  
Beta to Theta: 104.1 km  
Gamma to Delta: 64.1 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 184.1 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 69.6 km  
Gamma to Theta: 72.0 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 182.0 km  
Delta to Zeta: 43.9 km  
Delta to Theta: 69.1 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 138.2 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 117.3 km  
Zeta to Theta: 27.9 km  

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct route exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.  
Moreover, the inspection route must incorporate exactly one of two specified corridors: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed tour that visits every warehouse precisely once and concludes at the origin point.
